About me

I'm an aerospace engineer building a career in Formula 1 aerodynamics.

I studied Aerospace Engineering at the Universitat Politècnica de València, specialising in Aerospace Vehicles, and closed the degree with a thesis on the front and rear wings of a 2026 F1 car, graded 9.2/10.

At UPV I joined FSUPV, the university's Formula Student team, in the aerodynamics department: aero surfaces in Siemens NX, STAR-CCM+ runs automated with Java macros, and CFD correlated with track data at Circuito Ricardo Tormo. Today I'm on the MSc in Advanced Motorsport Engineering at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid.

Before motorsport I spent a year and a half at Air Nostrum, digitalising aircraft maintenance with automation, SQL and engineering dashboards used every day by a live airline.

Selected projects

The wing study that closed my degree, and the full aero package I'm building next.

BSc Thesis: Front & Rear Wing Design for a 2026 F1 Car ↗

Design and CFD optimisation of a multi-element front and rear wing under the FIA 2026 Technical Regulations, from 2D airfoil screening to a full-car study of the new active aero modes, Corner Mode (Z) and Straight Mode (X).

+42.8%front wing downforce
+20.9%rear wing downforce
−54.4%wing drag in X-mode
9.2/10grade
Full project page, coming soon

MSc Thesis: Full Aerodynamic Package of a 2026 F1 Car

In progress

Continuation of the BSc thesis at UPM: a complete aerodynamic package for a 2026-regulation car, adding a Venturi floor, rotating wheels and the transient switch between Z-mode and X-mode.

Less drag. More downforce.
